newsitem.title: USA: Suspect in Texas bank robberies nabbed, shoots self.
newsitem.headline: Suspect in Texas bank robberies nabbed, shoots self.

text.p: A man believed to have robbed at least 38 banks over seven years was in critical condition Wednesday after shooting himself in the head when cornered by police at the end of a high-speed chase, authorities said.

Police said they think the suspect, William Guess, a 46-year-old used car salesman from Temple, Texas, was the robber they had dubbed the Polo Shirt Bandit, accused of robbing banks in several Texas cities.
Police said Guess was chased by more than a dozen police cars after he allegedly robbed a Guaranty National Bank branch in northwest Houston Wednesday morning.
The chase ended when Guess rammed his car into another and emerged holding a .9 mm Russian-made pistol as police moved in, said Harris County Sheriff's Office Lt. Grace Hefner.

"As they approached, he had the gun in his hand and he told them 'I'm not going to hurt you and I have not hurt anyone.' He pulled the trigger and shot himself in the right temple," she told reporters. Guess was taken to a hospital where he had undergone surgery, police said.
The Polo Shirt Bandit earned his nickname because his usual attire, captured on many bank security cameras, consisted of a polo shirt, blue jeans, fake beard and baseball cap.
Thomas said Guess was wearing a polo shirt Wednesday and investigators found a fake beard and baseball cap in his car.

"I think we can say he probably is (the Polo Shirt Bandit), but I'm not going to say in fact (he is) right now," Thomas said. He said no charges had yet been filed against Guess, but that warrants were being obtained to search his home in Temple, which is in central Texas.

Police said the 38 robberies attributed to the Polo Shirt Bandit included only those pulled off in the Houston area. They said he was thought also to have robbed banks in other Texas cities like San Antonio, Austin and Waco.
Police recently stepped up patrols in northwest Houston because the Polo Shirt Bandit typically struck a bank in that area about every two months.
"He's been a nightmare. He's been a thorn in our side," Hefner said.
